subject: Clarification on mid-cycle invoice lines and ingest sampling evidence
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@nixta.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, billing@nixta.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected mid-cycle invoice increase — need allocation evidence

Hi Logan / Redwood billing team,

We just received the April invoice (attached) and noticed a ~45% increase on the "ingest" line versus our last two months. The invoice references 3.2M tokens for the period 2026-04-01 — 2026-04-20 but our internal telemetry shows ~1.9M.

Can you send the sampling logs and the per-tenant attribution you used to generate that line? We have a month-end procurement hold until we reconcile this discrepancy; billing@nixta.com is copied for PO coordination.

Attachment: nixta_invoice_202604.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Data Platforms
Nixta Labs

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@nixta.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle invoice increase — need allocation evidence

Hi Marta — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the surprise. I'm pulling the logs now. A few quick notes before we dig in:

- We run a weighted sampling for ingest attribution when traffic spikes are detected. That sampling runs at the edge aggregator and is later expanded to estimate total token counts.
- If you have a tenant/namespace ID you want us to prioritize in the export, share it and I'll include matching rows.

Ben — can you pull the raw sampling CSV and the expansion factors for Nixta (deal D-94823) for Apr 1–20 and drop them into the Drive link? Kimberly, can you review whether any mid-cycle rule changes (e.g., burst smoothing) were applied to Nixta's account?

I'll follow up with the CSV and a short reconciliation summary by EOD.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@nixta.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, billing@nixta.com
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle invoice increase — need allocation evidence

Hi Marta — attaching the sampling export and our expansion notes. Short summary below.

Attachment: sampling_logs-20260421.csv (csv)

Summary:
- Raw sampled requests (edge) for Nixta's API key ns: nixta-prod-3 show 195,402 sampled tokens between Apr 1–20.
- Expansion factor applied: 16.38x (this is conservative; it accounts for burst windows where we only sample 1/25 requests to limit edge overhead).
- Resulting estimated tokens: ~3.20M (matches the invoice line).

Why the difference vs your telemetry: your internal meter (per your note) reports 1.9M; we often see divergence when customers proxy requests through a gateway that aggregates or strips prompt tokens before reaching our SDK. Can you confirm whether Nixta's gateway performs request batching or token truncation before the call reaches the Redwood client?

If Nixta prefers, we can run a deterministic re-count by replaying the raw request IDs (we retained hashed request ids for 45 days) — this will take ~36–48 hours and requires a signed PO for replay compute. If the replay shows our estimate overshot, we'll apply a retroactive credit pro rata for the period.

Let us know how you'd like to proceed; Logan and I can coordinate the PO/redline.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marta Ruiz <marta@nixta.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@nixta.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle invoice increase — need allocation evidence

Thanks Ben — the CSV is helpful. A few points and next steps: 

- Nixta does perform request coalescing at the gateway (we batch short prompts to reduce latency) and we do some pre-filtering of prompts (system messages) before they reach the client. That likely explains some of the delta.
- We'd like Redwood to run the deterministic re-count for the Apr 1–20 window to be certain; please provide the PO/estimate and the SLAs for the replay (time to completion).
- In the meantime we'll release the procurement hold for the non-ingest lines to avoid downstream supplier delays, but the ingest line will remain in question until the replay completes.

Requested items:
1) PO estimate for deterministic replay (compute hours + any storage costs).
2) Expected completion ETA.
3) A proposed provisional credit policy if replay reduces the billed tokens (percent or formula).

If you can get the PO and ETA today, billing@nixta.com will start internal approvals.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Data Platforms
Nixta Labs
